answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring every new identity to dock at a public wharf and lock a pigment-colored basalt stake for 12 epochs before rewards. The stake returns only after the identity gathers independent peer attestations showing no shared-key patterns. A farm must lock fresh capital for each clone and wait the full period; if any clone is flagged by correlated attestation timing, the linked stake is burned. This multiplies capital and time cost per fake while adding detection risk that grows with farm size, making bulk faking far costlier than honest single-identity work.
